english_meaning: By One More Than the Previous One

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Calculating 95² in my head in under two seconds is impossible, Guru-ji!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Calculating 95 squared in under two seconds is impossible, Guru-ji!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Observe closely! By Ekādhikena Pūrveṇa—one more than 9 is 10. Simply multiply 9 × 10!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='95%'>Observe closely! By Ekadhikena Purvena—one more than 9 is 10. Simply multiply 9 times 10!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 9 × 10 is 90, and 5² is 25... so the answer is 9025?!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+4st'>9 times 10 is 90, and 5 squared is 25... so 9025?!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Precisely! Now prove your understanding for 45²: tap the number that is one more than 4!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Precisely! Now prove your understanding for 45 squared: tap the number that is one more than 4!</speak>

english_meaning: All from 9 and the Last from 10

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Multiplying 96 × 92 requires pen, paper, and too many steps!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Multiplying 96 times 92 requires pen, paper, and too many steps!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Anchor to Base 100! Their deficiencies are -4 and -8. Cross-subtract: 96 - 8 = 88!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Anchor to Base 100! Their deficiencies are minus 4 and minus 8. Cross-subtract: 96 minus 8 is 88!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: And the product of deficiencies (-4 × -8) is 32... making 8832!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>And the product of deficiencies minus 4 times minus 8 is 32... making 8832!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Masterful! For 98 × 97 with base deficiencies -2 and -3, tap the product: (-2 × -3)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Masterful! For 98 times 97 with deficiencies minus 2 and minus 3, tap the product of minus 2 and minus 3!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: How do we multiply arbitrary numbers like 23 × 12 without a standard long multiplication grid?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>How do we multiply arbitrary numbers like 23 times 12 without a standard long grid?</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: We cast three spatial rays: Right Vertical (3×2=6), Crosswise (2×2 + 3×1=7), Left Vertical (2×1=2)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>We cast three spatial rays: Right Vertical, Crosswise, and Left Vertical!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 2 | 7 | 6 combined gives 276 in a single line!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>2, 7, 6 combined gives 276 in a single line!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now compute the crosswise middle term for 31 × 21: (3×1 + 1×2)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now compute the crosswise middle term for 31 times 21!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Dividing polynomials like (x² + 7x + 12) ÷ (x + 3) seems like tedious algebra!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Dividing polynomials like x squared plus 7x plus 12 divided by x plus 3 seems tedious!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Transpose the divisor root: +3 becomes -3. Multiply and add down coefficients: 7 + (-3) = 4!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Transpose the divisor root: plus 3 becomes minus 3. Multiply and add down!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: The quotient is directly (x + 4) with zero remainder!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>The quotient is directly x plus 4 with zero remainder!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Transpose to solve 3x + 12 = 0: x = -12 ÷ 3. Tap the solution magnitude!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Transpose to solve 3x plus 12 equals 0: tap the magnitude of x!</speak>

english_meaning: When the Collection is the Same, it is Zero

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Solving (x + 2) + (x + 3) = (x + 1) + (x + 4) looks like a multi-step equation.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Solving this equation looks like a multi-step algebraic expansion.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Inspect the sums: LHS constant sum is 2 + 3 = 5. RHS constant sum is 1 + 4 = 5. Both sums match!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Inspect the sums! Both LHS and RHS constant sums equal 5!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: When the collection is the same, x equates directly to 0!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>When the collection is the same, x equates directly to 0!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Immediate insight! Tap the zero key to confirm Śūnyaṁ!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Immediate insight! Tap the zero key to confirm Shunyam!</speak>

english_meaning: If One is in Ratio, the Other is Zero

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: For 2x + 3y = 6 and 4x + 6y = 12, elimination requires multiplying across!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>For simultaneous equations, standard elimination takes multiple steps!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Notice the x-coefficients (2:4 = 1:2) match the constant ratio (6:12 = 1:2). Therefore, y is 0!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>The x-ratio matches the constant ratio! Therefore, y is directly zero!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: If y = 0, then 2x = 6, which makes x = 3 instantly!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>If y equals 0, then 2x equals 6, which makes x equals 3 instantly!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Confirm the value of x when 2x = 6!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Confirm the value of x when 2x equals 6!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: For 45x - 23y = 113 and 23x - 45y = 91, large coefficients make substitution difficult.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>For cross-symmetric equations, large coefficients make substitution difficult.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Add them: 68x - 68y = 204 $\implies$ x - y = 3. Subtract them: 22x + 22y = 22 $\implies$ x + y = 1!

math_overlay.expression: Add: x - y = 3,  Sub: x + y = 1

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Add them to get x minus y equals 3! Subtract them to get x plus y equals 1!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Adding (x - y = 3) and (x + y = 1) gives 2x = 4 $\implies$ x = 2, y = -1!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Adding both reduced equations gives 2x equals 4, so x is 2 and y is minus 1!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Tap the value of x (2x = 4) to cement the method!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Tap the value of x to cement the method!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Factoring x² + 6x - 16 by trial and error is tricky.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Factoring quadratic expressions by trial and error is tricky.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Complete the square! Half of 6 is 3, and 3² is 9. Add 9 to both sides: (x + 3)² = 25!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Complete the square! Add 9 to both sides: x plus 3 squared equals 25!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Taking the square root gives x + 3 = 5 $\implies$ x = 2!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Taking the square root gives x plus 3 equals 5, so x is 2!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: What is the square root of 25? Tap the answer!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>What is the square root of 25? Tap the answer!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Finding the vertex turning point of 2x² - 8x + 5 usually takes full derivative formulas!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Finding the vertex turning point of quadratics usually takes full formulas!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Apply Calana-Kalanābhyām! Differentiate mentally: 2(2x) - 8 = 0 $\implies$ 4x = 8.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Apply the differential sutra! 4x minus 8 equals 0!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 4x = 8 $\implies$ x = 2! That gives the critical point in two seconds!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>4x equals 8, so x is 2! That gives the critical point in two seconds!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Solve for the turning point x: 4x = 8. Tap the root!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Solve for the turning point x: 4x equals 8. Tap the root!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Squaring near-base numbers like 94² in my head seems prone to errors.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Squaring near-base numbers like 94 squared in my head seems difficult.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Deficiency from 100 is 6. Lessen by deficiency: 94 - 6 = 88. Square the deficiency: 6² = 36!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Deficiency from 100 is 6. Lessen 94 by 6 to get 88, and square 6 to get 36!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 88 and 36 combine into 8836 immediately!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>88 and 36 combine into 8836 immediately!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: For 97² (deficiency 3): 97 - 3 = 94. What is 3²?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>For 97 squared with deficiency 3: 97 minus 3 is 94. What is 3 squared?</speak>

english_meaning: Specific and General / Part and Whole

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Factoring biquadratic expressions like x⁴ - 10x² + 9 feels overwhelming.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Factoring biquadratics like x to the fourth minus 10x squared plus 9 feels overwhelming.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Break the whole into parts! Let u = x². The equation reduces to u² - 10u + 9 = (u - 1)(u - 9)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Break the whole into parts! Substitute u equals x squared to factor easily!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: The roots are ±1 and ±3 without any cubic or quartic formulas!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>The roots are plus-or-minus 1 and plus-or-minus 3!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Tap the positive root corresponding to x² = 9!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Tap the positive root corresponding to x squared equals 9!</speak>

english_meaning: The Remainders by the Last Digit

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Converting fractions like 1/7 into exact repeating decimals takes forever by long division.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Converting fractions like 1 over 7 into repeating decimals takes forever.</speak>
<speak>Track the remainders! Each remainder generates the next decimal digit immediately!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: The digits 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 form the cyclic pattern instantly!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>The digits form the cyclic pattern 142857 instantly!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: What is the remainder when 10 is divided by 7? Tap the remainder!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>What is the remainder when 10 is divided by 7? Tap the remainder!</speak>

english_meaning: The Ultimate and Twice the Penultimate

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Rational equations like 1/(x+2) + 1/(x+3) = 1/(x+1) + 1/(x+4) take messy cross-multiplications.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Rational equations like this take messy cross-multiplications.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Penultimate sum is (2+3)=5, Ultimate sum is (1+4)=5. When equal, set the numerator sum to 0: 2x + 5 = 0!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Penultimate and ultimate sums match! Simply set 2x plus 5 equals 0!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 2x = -5 gives x = -2.5 without expanding quadratic denominators!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>2x equals minus 5 gives x equals minus 2.5 in one step!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: For 2x + 6 = 0, tap the magnitude of x (|-3| = 3)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>For 2x plus 6 equals 0, tap the magnitude of x!</speak>

english_meaning: By One Less Than the Previous One

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Multiplying 46 × 99 mentally sounds difficult without a calculator.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Multiplying 46 times 99 mentally sounds difficult without a calculator.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Reduce 46 by one: 46 - 1 = 45. Then subtract 45 from 99: 99 - 45 = 54!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Reduce 46 by one to get 45. Then subtract 45 from 99 to get 54!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 45 and 54 together make 4554 instantly!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>45 and 54 together make 4554 instantly!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: For 73 × 99, reduce 73 by one. Tap the units digit of 72!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>For 73 times 99, reduce 73 by one. Tap the units digit of 72!</speak>

english_meaning: The Product of the Sum is the Sum of the Products

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: How do I verify if (x + 2)(x + 3) = x² + 5x + 6 without recalculating every term?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>How do I verify polynomial factor expansions without recalculating every term?</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Set x = 1! Factor sum product: (1+2)(1+3) = 3 × 4 = 12. Expansion sum: 1 + 5 + 6 = 12. They match!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Set x equals 1! Both the factor sum product and expansion sum equal 12!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 12 equals 12 proves the expansion is 100% accurate in one check!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>12 equals 12 proves the expansion is completely accurate!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: For (x + 1)(x + 2), what is the factor sum product at x = 1: (2 × 3)?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>What is the factor sum product at x equals 1 for x plus 1 times x plus 2?</speak>

english_meaning: The Factors of the Sum is the Sum of the Factors

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Factorizing 2x² + 5x + 2 requires checking multiple product pairs.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Factorizing 2x squared plus 5x plus 2 requires checking multiple product pairs.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Evaluate Sc(expression): 2 + 5 + 2 = 9. Sc(factors) must multiply to 9: (2(1)+1)(1+2) = 3 × 3 = 9!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Expression coefficient sum is 9. Factor sums multiply to 3 times 3 equals 9!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: (2x + 1)(x + 2) is verified as the true factor pair!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>2x plus 1 times x plus 2 is verified as the true factor pair!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: You have mastered all 16 Vedic Sutras, Shishya! Tap 9 to begin your grand master trial!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>You have mastered all 16 Vedic Sutras, Shishya! Tap 9 to begin your trial!</speak>
